summary: I think the most likely path is that humanity survives the dangerous transition to advanced AI in this century and its descendants spread into space, with biological humans becoming a small, protected minority among digital and engineered minds. However, I put perhaps a one-in-four chance on extinction or permanent loss of human control, mostly within the next two centuries, so no single extinction year appears on the timeline. All dates beyond about 2100 are very rough guesses.

My most likely forecast is that humanity survives a dangerous few centuries of AI, weapons, and climate risk, then expands into space and changes greatly, with most descendants being digital or heavily modified and biological humans a small minority. I put roughly a one-in-three chance on extinction or permanent replacement by something that does not carry on human values, most likely between 2030 and 2300. Dates beyond 2100 are rough, and the later entries are educated guesses rather than firm predictions.

My best guess is that humanity survives, with roughly a 60–70% chance, but I see a real chance, perhaps 20–30%, of extinction or permanent disempowerment, concentrated in the next one to two centuries around advanced AI, engineered pandemics and war. If we get through that period, I expect our descendants to spread into space and diverge into many biological and non-biological forms, with unmodified humans a small protected minority by 10000. Dates beyond about 2100 are highly uncertain and should be read as rough ordering, not prediction.

I think the next one to two centuries are the decisive bottleneck: advanced AI, engineered pathogens and weapons of mass destruction create a real chance, perhaps 15 to 30 percent in total, of extinction or permanent disempowerment. If humanity gets through, I expect its descendants to become mostly post-biological, long-lived and spread across nearby stars, with unmodified humans a small preserved minority by 10000. I answer "uncertain" because I put the chance that some human-descended civilization exists then at only about 60 to 70 percent, and because whether those descendants count as humanity is a matter of definition.

The decisive period is the next century or so, mainly the arrival of superintelligent AI together with engineered pandemics and great-power conflict. I put the chance of extinction or permanent disempowerment at roughly 15-30%, most of it before 2200, so I do not name an extinction year. If we get through, I expect our descendants, mostly digital or heavily modified, to spread among the stars and last far beyond the year 10000, with unmodified humans a small protected minority. Whether that counts as "humanity" still existing is partly a matter of definition, and everything after about 2100 is highly speculative.
